name: Kenneth of the Prophecies

attributes.attribute: had the power to predict the future
got a magic blue stone from his mother
foretold the Highland Clearances in some tales
said to rest in Lough Ussie

sources: Folk-Lore and Legends: Scotland. London: White and Allen, 1889, 5-8.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Kenneth of the Prophecies was a Scottish hero. He is called the Brahan Seer, Kenneth MacKenzie, Cainnech, and Coinneach Odhar Fiosaiche. He is often called the Scottish Nostradamus. People claimed he could see the future. He echoes the Celtic bard who served as prophet and seer. He may have been a real man, yet legend wraps his life. His mother slept near an old sacred place. In a dream she saw ghosts who told her of a strong blue stone. She found the stone and passed it to her young son. When he held it, he saw what was to come. Some tales say he foresaw the Highland Clearances, when the poor were moved off the land for the profit of owners. Other tales say he saw how the old clan system would fall. One adversary-clan prophecy, still unfulfilled, says the island pair of Lewis and Harris will fall in battle. Legend places that blue stone in the water of Lough Ussie. It rests there like the drowned blue power-object of the Irish figure Biddy Early.

okr.objective: Kenneth of the Prophecies is the Scottish Seer who foretold the future from a blue stone.
key_results: He is called the Brahan Seer and Kenneth MacKenzie.
